1930年代，美國吉他製造商為與鼓等較響樂器競爭，嘗試以喇叭擴大吉他音量。193: In the 1930s American guitar makers tried to make the guitar louder through a horn, to compete with louder instruments such as the drums. In 1936 Gibson brought out the first mass-produced semi-hollow guitar, based on the traditional jazz archtop, with f-holes and a Charlie Christian single-coil magnetic pickup; its clear tone was taken up by jazz players. In 1949 Gibson brought out its first models with built-in pickups, regarded as fully electric semi-hollow guitars. In 1958 Gibson added a solid wood centre block and developed the semi-hollow body, which reduced feedback and allowed more gain; Rickenbacker also began making them that year, and brands such as Gretsch kept producing them.

半空心吉他常見於爵士、藍調與早期搖滾的電吉他編制，也出現在流行、民謠與部分搖滾分: The semi-acoustic guitar is common in the electric guitar line-ups of jazz, blues and early rock, and it also appears in pop, folk and some branches of rock. Through its pickups it is plugged into a guitar amplifier, and in ensembles that want a warm, clean tone it can take the rhythm or the lead; at high volume in a large venue it may feed back, and later rock players turned that feedback into an effect. A demonstration can be understood from the electric guitar part in a jazz, blues or rock band.
半空心吉他琴身以木製空心或半空心結構為主，部分型號具貫穿琴身長度與深度的實心木塊: The body of the semi-acoustic guitar is mainly a hollow or semi-hollow wooden structure; some models have a solid block running the length and depth of the body, with the bridge fixed to the block rather than to the resonating top; there are also chambered designs in which cavities and soundholes are cut from a solid blank. The top may be of laminated wood, and electromagnetic pickups are fitted; the source does not state the particular materials of the pickups, fingerboard, neck, strings or hardware.
半空心吉他音色溫潤而富有穿透力，兼具溫暖與清晰的特質。相比實心電吉他的銳利與冷冽: The semi-acoustic guitar has a warm timbre that carries well, both warm and clear. Beside the sharp, cold sound of a solid-body electric guitar it is softer and fuller; beside the bright openness of a folk guitar it has more reserve and maturity. Its hollow body lets the strings resonate naturally as they vibrate, so the bass is full and deep and the middle and upper register clear and strong. This distinctive resonance gives it a wide range: it can produce the roundness of jazz and also carry the emotional tension of the blues. Because it combines electric transduction with wooden resonance, its timbre falls between the acoustic and the electric guitar, with a character all its own, so that in a band it keeps its personality while blending naturally.
半空心吉他（亦稱空心體電吉他）屬弦鳴樂器，起源於美國，需接吉他音箱演奏，琴身全空: The semi-acoustic guitar (also called the hollow-body electric guitar) is a chordophone that originated in the United States; it is played through a guitar amplifier, and its body is wholly or partly hollow with at least one electromagnetic pickup. Construction falls into fully hollow, thinline hollow, and semi-hollow with a solid centre block; the last reduces feedback and suits higher volume and gain. It differs from an acoustic guitar to which amplification has merely been added, and it is used mainly in jazz, blues and early rock, and also in pop, folk, rockabilly and psychedelic rock.
